key_insight: Disagreement between fixed numerical rewards and expert preferences can reveal promising materials that automated scoring overlooks.
engineering_relevance: Expert-informed generative models could broaden materials searches beyond rigid targets, including electronic flat bands, synthesizability, and phonon properties.
method: Compare expert judgments with a numerical electronic-bandwidth score.
Learn expert preferences from pairwise material comparisons.
Use learned preferences to guide a crystal diffusion model.
evidence_signal: Expert–score disagreements were systematic and not explained by an estimated 5% labeling-error rate; learned preferences favored reported partially flat-band compounds KCo2As2 and CoGa that the numerical score would discard.
watch_item: Preference-guided candidates still require independent validation; expert agreement alone does not establish synthesizability or useful material performance.
paper_title: Reward misalignment as an opportunity for materials discovery
